title: Why "and more" is lazy marketing: just say what you are and own it
summary: Jason Cohen argues that "and more" in business names and signage is usually untrue, dilutes passion, and signals an incomplete message. Instead, state specifically what you are, be passionate about it, and make sure your ideal customer understands.

principles.text: "And more" is a weak declaration that your message is incomplete; say what you are instead.
principles.quote: In the end, "and more" is a weak declaration that your message is incomplete.

principles.text: Specific, singular passion beats vague breadth; "and more" dilutes an otherwise compelling message.
principles.quote: Look how the phrase "and more" dilutes this otherwise incredible message.

principles.text: Replace filler with enthusiasm: show you are fully committed to your niche.
principles.quote: Instead of wasting time with a useless, incorrect phrase, why not punch up the enthusiasm?

principles.text: Non-committal phrases fail to interest, excite, or get people through the door.
principles.quote: non-committal phrases don't get me interested, don't get me excited, and don't get me in the door.

principles.text: Listing extra categories rarely wins over people uninterested in your core offer.
principles.quote: The person who is completely uninterested in bed and bath products is unlikely to be interested in air fresheners and cutlery.

principles.text: Own your identity and make sure your ideal customer persona gets it; the rest follows.
principles.quote: So forget about "more."  Just say what you are.  Own it.  Make sure Carol gets it and the rest will follow.
